info.name: RideLink Complete Microservices Demo
info.description: End-to-end Account, Driver, Ride lifecycle and Payment proxy workflow. Normal payment calls go through Ride. The Fare request is explicitly internal and requires a locally supplied service key.

request.description: Creates a fresh fictional passenger account on every run.
Authenticated account/profile operation. Confirms the passenger JWT is valid.
accountId is taken from the authenticated Driver account, not the request body.

exec: pm.test('Driver profile belongs to logged-in account', function () { pm.expect(String(body.accountId)).to.eql(pm.environment.get('driverAccountId')); });

request.description: The Ride service reserves an available driver automatically when a booking is submitted.

exec: pm.test('At least one available driver is returned', function () { pm.expect(rows.length).to.be.above(0); });

item.name: 3. Ride Lifecycle
item.description: Request persists REQUESTED, reserves an available driver synchronously, and returns ASSIGNED. Then run accept, start, complete in order.

item.name: Request Ride (response is ASSIGNED after automatic reservation)

request.description: Ride is persisted as REQUESTED before Driver reservation; this synchronous endpoint returns after successful reservation as ASSIGNED.

exec: pm.test('Booking automatically reserves a driver', function () { pm.expect(body.status).to.eql('ASSIGNED'); });
pm.test('Ride accepted by assigned driver', function () { pm.expect(body.status).to.eql('ACCEPTED'); });

item.name: Calculate Fare Estimate (internal API key required)

request.description: Payment's Fare API is protected by its internal service key. Set paymentServiceKey locally from your local credential file to run this request. Do not export an environment containing the populated secret.

exec: pm.test('Fare calculation uses configured formula', function () { pm.expect(body.totalFare).to.eql(22); });
pm.test('Estimate refers to the completed demo ride', function () { pm.expect(String(body.rideId)).to.eql(pm.environment.get('rideId')); });

item.name: 5. Payment (via Ride)
item.description: Payment actions use JWT-protected Ride proxy endpoints; no internal Payment key is sent by Postman.

request.description: User-facing payment operation through Ride. The internal Payment key is added by Ride's PaymentClient.

exec: pm.test('Payment belongs to completed ride', function () { pm.expect(String(body.rideId)).to.eql(pm.environment.get('rideId')); });
pm.test('Payment is linked to this ride', function () { pm.expect(String(body.rideId)).to.eql(pm.environment.get('rideId')); });
pm.test('Receipt belongs to this ride', function () { pm.expect(String(body.rideId)).to.eql(pm.environment.get('rideId')); });

item.name: 6. Negative Scenarios
item.description: Run after Account tokens and main ride are captured. The folder creates a second assigned ride for pre-completion, authorization, invalid-transition and cancellation checks.

request.description: Creates an additional assigned ride so authorization and pre-completion negative cases do not disrupt the main lifecycle demo.

item.name: Wrong Role - Passenger Tries to Accept
Wrong Owner - Read Another Passenger Ride Payment

request.description: Run after Payment - Create Payment for Completed Ride. Payment Service enforces one payment per ride; the Ride proxy returns 409.

exec: pm.test('Ride was cancelled and driver released', function () { pm.expect(body.status).to.eql('CANCELLED'); pm.expect(body.releasePending).to.eql(false); });
